description: Phase 7F labelled query set for the card router (sap_m2c_card_v1): new in-domain queries, clearly out-of-domain queries, and ambiguous queries that are excluded from the decision. The Phase 4 (50) and Phase 5 (54) queries are used unchanged, with their recorded labels, as the main in-domain population; they are not copied into this file.

authorship.authored_by: the AI coding agent (Arena.ai Agent Mode), by hand, in the Phase 7F session; no human author and no human domain expert
authorship.automated_generation: none: no LLM API call, no sampling script, no paraphrasing tool and no template generator produced these queries; each was typed individually
authorship.caveat: the agent is itself a language model, so these queries are NOT human-written. The statement 'not generated by an LLM' therefore cannot be made; the accurate statement is 'authored directly by an AI agent without a generation pipeline'. This limits how far the evidence generalises (a human-written set should be added before any threshold is trusted).
authorship.written_before_evaluation: yes: this file was written, saved to the workspace (its sha256 is recorded by the evaluator) before any of its queries was embedded or routed. The agent had seen only the card texts, the Phase 4/5 data and the five legacy out-of-domain questions of Phase 7E
authorship.labels_changed_after_retrieval: never; the evaluator records the sha256 of this file and a test fails if the labels change

labelling_criteria.in_domain: A card's 'What it covers' statement names the process or object the query asks about, so that card is an appropriate pointer. expected_source_ids and the quoted evidence come from the card text only.
labelling_criteria.out_of_domain: No card's title or 'What it covers' statement covers the subject. Includes unrelated subjects, other software, other SAP areas, utility-industry topics the cards do not cover, and vocabulary traps. Plausible user questions are included, not only nonsense.
labelling_criteria.ambiguous_excluded: The card text alone does not settle whether a card would answer. Reported separately and never used to choose or evaluate a threshold. They are not relabelled after retrieval.
labelling_criteria.in_domain_independence: new in-domain queries were written to differ from the card wording (max 3 contiguous words shared with any card's embedding_text), and differ from every Phase 4 and Phase 5 query

split_rule: For each label group, order the pooled queries as: Phase 4 (by question id), Phase 5 (by query id), 7F new queries (by id). The item at 0-based position i of its group is 'dev' if i is even and 'test' if i is odd. The ambiguous queries and the five legacy out-of-domain questions are not split.

decision_rule.score: rank-1 cosine SIMILARITY = 1 - cosine distance, as returned by the unchanged dense router (no threshold, k=29, rank 1 only)
decision_rule.populations: in-domain = Phase 4 (50) + Phase 5 (54) + 7F in-domain; out-of-domain = 7F out_of_domain (the clear ones only)
decision_rule.C1_sample_adequacy: n_in_domain >= 100, n_out_of_domain >= 50, and at least 25 out-of-domain queries in each of dev and test
decision_rule.C2_separation_pooled: AUROC (probability that a random in-domain rank-1 similarity exceeds a random out-of-domain one, ties 0.5) >= 0.90 AND some threshold t has in-domain refusal rate <= 0.05 AND out-of-domain acceptance rate <= 0.20 on the pooled set
decision_rule.C3_held_out: t* = on DEV only: among candidate thresholds (midpoints between adjacent distinct DEV scores) with DEV in-domain refusal rate <= 0.05, the one with the lowest DEV out-of-domain acceptance rate (ties: the lowest t). On TEST, t* must give in-domain refusal rate <= 0.10 and out-of-domain acceptance rate <= 0.25
decision_rule.verdict: a threshold is justified only if C1, C2 and C3 all hold, and even then it is indicative (small sample, agent-authored). Otherwise no threshold is justified and min_cosine stays None
decision_rule.not_gates: ambiguous queries, the five legacy out-of-domain questions, the gap rank1-rank2, and per-category figures are descriptive only
decision_rule.acceptance_semantics: a query is accepted when rank-1 similarity >= t (inclusive); refused when below
